item.title: Space Capsule vs Apple Cabin: Which One Fits Your Project?
item.description:
Space Capsule vs Apple Cabin: Which One Fits Your Project?

Space capsules and apple cabins are both attractive options for tourism and accommodation projects, but they usually serve slightly different positioning goals.

Choose Space Capsule When

  • You want a stronger futuristic image
  • The room itself should become a marketing highlight
  • The project needs a premium, highly visual accommodation unit
  • You want to emphasize panoramic experience and product identity

item.title: How to Choose the Right Prefab Unit for a Resort or Glamping Project
item.description:
How to Choose the Right Prefab Unit for a Resort or Glamping Project

When an overseas buyer starts a resort or glamping project, the first mistake is often choosing a model before clarifying the business goal.
The better sequence is to define the guest experience first, then match the product family to that goal.

Step 1. Define the Positioning of the Project

Ask these questions first:

  • Is the project premium, mid-range, or budget-sensitive?
  • Is the main selling point the room experience, the scenery, or the price?
  • Do guests expect a design-led unit or a more natural cabin atmosphere?
  • Is fast deployment more important than architectural uniqueness?

Step 2. Match the Positioning to the Product Family

Space Capsule

Best for projects that need a highly recognizable room type and a stronger visual identity.

item.title: E7 Space Capsule
item.description:
The E7 is the larger premium model in the XC space capsule range.
It is designed for buyers who want to move from a compact capsule room into a more spacious suite-style accommodation product.

Size Class Approx. 11500 × 3300 × 3200 mm
Reference Area About 38 square meters
Typical Occupancy About 2 to 4 guests
Ask About E7 Open E7 drawing Back to Space Capsule family

Why Buyers Move Up to E7

  • The larger footprint supports higher-value room planning.
  • It is better suited to suite-style hospitality concepts.
  • It gives resort buyers more flexibility for family or premium-stay positioning.
  • It helps projects that need a more spacious room type without leaving the capsule product family.

E7 Snapshot

Item Reference information
Product model E7 Space Capsule
External dimensions 11500 mm × 3300 mm × 3200 mm
Reference floor area 38.0 m²
Reference occupancy 2 to 4 persons
Reference power 10 KW without underfloor heating / 15 KW with underfloor heating
Reference weight About 8 tons
Air-conditioning reference 2 sets listed in the original configuration sheet

Configuration Highlights

  • Integrated galvanized steel structure
  • Aviation aluminum outer shell with fluorocarbon finish
  • Low-E insulating glass system
  • Polyurethane insulation system
  • Smart lock and integrated lighting logic
  • Bathroom and utility systems for hospitality use
  • Larger suite-style room planning than E5

Best-Fit Projects

  • premium resort suites
  • scenic-area family rooms
  • boutique hospitality clusters
  • projects that need a larger room type than E5 or E6

Model Comparison

  • Choose E5 when compact premium rooms are enough and balcony appeal matters.
  • Choose E6 when you want more indoor living function at compact length.
  • Choose E7 when room size and suite-style positioning are the top priority.

Planning Note for Export Buyers

The E7 is a larger unit than E5 or E6, so transport route, unloading conditions, and site access should be reviewed early in the inquiry stage.

item.title: K-Type vs T-Type Prefab Houses: Full Comparison & Use Cases
item.description:
🏗 1. K-Type Prefab House (K-Style House)

🔹 Name Origin:

The “K” may come from the word “Knock-down”, referring to modular, dismountable construction, or it may simply denote a standard modular span unit.

🔹 Features: • Modular design: Each “K” represents a standard module, typically 1.82 meters wide. • The size is defined by the number of modules. For example, a 3K x 6K house measures 5.46m wide (1.82 x 3) and 10.92m long (1.82 x 6). • Optional single or double-slope roof • Low cost and quick installation • Can be stacked 2–3 stories

What is a Mobile House?

Keywords: mobile house, mobile home, modular home, prefabricated house, affordable housing, manufactured home

Discover everything you need to know about mobile houses.

A mobile house, commonly known as a mobile home, is a prefabricated structure built in a factory setting and transported to a site for use as a permanent or temporary residence. These homes are constructed on a permanently attached chassis, allowing them to be moved to different locations as needed. Unlike traditional site-built homes, mobile houses are designed to offer flexibility and affordability without compromising on quality. History and Evolution
